spans.s:
Kaca
(‘[One] who shines [by तपस्]’)
------------------------------------------
The देवस् and the असुरस् (gods and demons) were eternal enemies. They were guided in their deeds and dealings by their preceptors, बृहस्पति and शुक्राचार्य.
Śukrācārya knew the science of mṛtasañjīvanī (bringing the dead back to life) whereas बृहस्पति did not. So, the gods sent कच, बृहस्पति’s son, to शुक्राचार्य as a Vedic student, to somehow get a knowledge of that science. Having got scent of their plan असुरस् managed to kill him. However, at the earnest entreaties of his dear daughter Devayānī who had fallen in love with कच, शुक्राचार्य brought him back to life. The असुरस् who would not give up so easily, managed to kill कच once again, burnt his body and surreptitiously fed शुक्राचार्य with wine—of which he was very fond of—mixed with the ashes of कच’s body. When Devayānī became inconsolable at this tragedy, शुक्राचार्य revived कच in his abdomen, taught the mṛtasañjīvanī science to him and requested him to come out and also save his own life. कच did as directed.
Having succeeded in getting what he wanted, he returned to his ड़थेर् बृहस्पति, flatly rejecting the मर्रिअगे proposal of Devayānī, since she was like a sister to him, being the daughter of his गुरु.
